lessons.title: Cardinal Directions and Turns
lessons.concept: Direction sense uses the four main (cardinal) directions: North, South, East, West, and the four sub-directions: North-East, North-West, South-East, South-West. Left/right turns depend on the direction you are currently facing, not on a fixed map unless stated.
lessons.formula: Facing North: left->West, right->East. Facing East: left->North, right->South. Facing South: left->East, right->West. Facing West: left->South, right->North.
lessons.worked_example: A person faces North and turns right: now faces East. From East turns right again: now faces South. Turning left from South leads to East.
mistakes: Taking left/right from viewer's perspective instead of the person's facing direction
Confusing clockwise/anticlockwise effects with left/right when facing differs
Mixing up East and West after multiple turns

lessons.title: Tracing Stepwise Movement
lessons.concept: To solve movement problems, track position and facing direction after each step in order. Draw a rough diagram or use coordinates mentally: moving North increases vertical position, South decreases it, East increases horizontal, West decreases it.
lessons.formula: Net displacement components: East-West = (total East - total West), North-South = (total North - total South).
lessons.worked_example: Ravi walks 5 km East, turns left and walks 3 km North, then turns left and walks 2 km West. Net East = 5-2 = 3 km, Net North = 3 km. He is 3 km East and 3 km North of start (facing West at end).
mistakes: Forgetting that a turn changes facing direction for the next move
Adding distances in opposite directions instead of subtracting

lessons.title: Distance vs Shortest Distance
lessons.concept: Total distance is the sum of all path lengths traveled. Shortest distance (displacement magnitude) is the straight-line distance from start to end point. When net movement forms a right-angled triangle, use the Pythagorean theorem.
lessons.formula: If net East-West = x and net North-South = y, shortest distance = sqrt(x^2 + y^2).
lessons.worked_example: A person walks 6 km North and then 8 km East. Total distance = 14 km. Shortest distance from start = sqrt(6^2 + 8^2) = sqrt(36 + 64) = sqrt(100) = 10 km.
mistakes: Confusing total path distance with shortest straight-line distance
Applying Pythagoras to non-perpendicular components without resolving them first

practice.question: A man is facing North. He turns right. Which direction is he facing now?
practice.explanation: When facing North, a right turn leads to East.

practice.question: A person faces East, turns left, then turns left again. Which direction is he facing now?
practice.explanation: Facing East, first left turn -> North. Facing North, second left turn -> West.
practice.provenance: Authored original practice item; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

practice.question: Rita walks 4 km North and then 3 km East. How far is she from the starting point (shortest distance)?
practice.explanation: North and East are perpendicular. Shortest distance = sqrt(4^2 + 3^2) = sqrt(16 + 9) = sqrt(25) = 5 km.
practice.provenance: Authored original practice item; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

practice.question: A boy walks 10 m South, turns right and walks 6 m, then turns right and walks 10 m. How far and in which direction is he from the starting point?
practice.explanation: Starts facing South (implied by first move): walks 10 m South. Turns right from South -> faces West, walks 6 m. Turns right from West -> faces North, walks 10 m. Net South-North = 10-10 = 0, net West = 6 m. So he is 6 m West of start.
practice.provenance: Authored original practice item; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

practice.question: If you are facing West, which direction will be to your left?
practice.explanation: When facing West, left side points to South and right side points to North.
practice.provenance: Authored original practice item; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

questions.question: A man walks 5 km North, then turns right and walks 5 km, then turns right and walks 5 km. How far is he from the starting point and in which direction?
questions.explanation: Walk 5 km North. Turn right from North -> East, walk 5 km. Turn right from East -> South, walk 5 km. Net North-South = 5-5 = 0, net East = 5 km. He is 5 km East of the starting point.
questions.provenance: Authored original question; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

questions.question: Starting from a point, Meena walks 12 m towards North, turns left and walks 5 m, then turns left and walks 12 m. What is the shortest distance between her final position and the starting point?
questions.explanation: 12 m North, left from North -> West 5 m, left from West -> South 12 m. Net North-South = 12-12 = 0, net West = 5 m. Shortest distance = 5 m.
questions.provenance: Authored original question; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

questions.question: A person starts facing South, turns right, walks 4 km, turns left, walks 3 km. Which direction is he facing at the end?
questions.explanation: Initially facing South. Right turn from South -> faces West and walks 4 km. Left turn from West -> faces South and walks 3 km. Final facing direction is South.
questions.provenance: Authored original question; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

questions.question: Karan walks 8 km East, then 6 km South. What is the shortest distance from his starting point?
questions.explanation: East and South movements are perpendicular. Shortest distance = sqrt(8^2 + 6^2) = sqrt(64 + 36) = sqrt(100) = 10 km.

questions.question: A girl walks 7 m West, turns left and walks 4 m, turns left and walks 7 m. How far is she from the starting point?
questions.explanation: 7 m West. Left from West -> South, 4 m. Left from South -> East, 7 m. Net West-East = 7-7 = 0, net South = 4 m. She is 4 m from the starting point.
